claims.claim: Hesychius of Jerusalem was a presbyter (priest) of the Church of Jerusalem.
Hesychius of Jerusalem was renowned as a theologian, biblical commentator, and preacher in the Eastern Church.
Hesychius was recognized by 429 as the pre-eminent biblical interpreter and teacher of the church in Jerusalem and Palestine.
Homilia ii de Hypapante was written in Greek at Jerusalem in the 410s or 420s.
The homily was preached on the feast of Hypapante (the Presentation of Jesus in the Temple), celebrated on 14 February at the Martyrion (Golgotha) in Jerusalem.
The homily consists of biblical exegesis focusing on the doctrine of Christ's incarnation.
The homily contains extensive references to Mary, the Mother of Christ.
The work survives in manuscript and was published in Migne's Patrologia Graeca, though a comprehensive critical edition of the homilies was published by Michel Aubineau in 1978.
Hesychius is credited with the earliest known liturgical addresses on the Virgin Mary.
Hesychius played a prominent role in the 5th-century controversy on the nature of Christ and was acclaimed as having annotated the whole of sacred Scripture.
